hints: Translate 'decreasing at a rate proportional to $Ne^{-0.02t}$' into a differential equation with a negative proportionality constant.
Solve for $k$ and insert it into the model.
walkthrough:
Translate the statement that the population decreases at a rate proportional to $N\mathrm{e}^{-0.02t}$ into a differential equation:
$$\dfrac{\mathrm{d}N}{\mathrm{d}t} = -k N\mathrm{e}^{-0.02t} \quad (\text{where } k > 0)$$

Substitute the given initial conditions $t = 0$, $N = 1000$, and $\dfrac{\mathrm{d}N}{\mathrm{d}t} = -10$:
$$-10 = -k(1000)\mathrm{e}^0$$
$$-10 = -1000k \implies k = \dfrac{10}{1000} = 0.01$$

Substitute $k = 0.01$ into the differential equation:
$$\dfrac{\mathrm{d}N}{\mathrm{d}t} = -0.01\mathrm{e}^{-0.02t}N$$
This confirms the given differential equation.

hints: Separate the model from part (i) as $dN/N=-0.01e^{-0.02t}dt$.
Integrate both sides; the time integral gains a factor $-1/0.02$.
Apply $N=1000$ at $t=0$ to determine the constant or use definite limits.
Set $N=800$, isolate $e^{-0.02t}$, then take logarithms to solve for $t$ in weeks.
walkthrough:
Separate variables in the differential equation $\dfrac{\mathrm{d}N}{\mathrm{d}t} = -0.01\mathrm{e}^{-0.02t}N$:
$$\dfrac{1}{N}\,\mathrm{d}N = -0.01\mathrm{e}^{-0.02t}\,\mathrm{d}t$$

Integrate both sides:
$$\int \dfrac{1}{N}\,\mathrm{d}N = \int -0.01\mathrm{e}^{-0.02t}\,\mathrm{d}t$$
$$\ln N = -0.01\left(\dfrac{\mathrm{e}^{-0.02t}}{-0.02}\right) + C = \dfrac{0.01}{0.02}\mathrm{e}^{-0.02t} + C = 0.5\mathrm{e}^{-0.02t} + C$$

Use the initial condition $t = 0$ when $N = 1000$ to find $C$:
$$\ln 1000 = 0.5\mathrm{e}^0 + C = 0.5 + C$$
$$C = \ln 1000 - 0.5$$

Substitute $C$ back to obtain the particular solution:
$$\ln N = 0.5\mathrm{e}^{-0.02t} + \ln 1000 - 0.5$$
$$\ln\left(\dfrac{N}{1000}\right) = 0.5\left(\mathrm{e}^{-0.02t} - 1\right)$$

Take the natural logarithm of both sides:
$$-0.02t = \ln(0.553713) \approx -0.591104$$
$$t = \dfrac{-0.591104}{-0.02} \approx 29.5552$$

hints: Use the solved relation from part (ii) and take the limit as $t\to\infty$.
Since $e^{-0.02t}\to0$, simplify the limiting logarithmic equation and exponentiate to identify the positive limiting population.
walkthrough:
Examine the limiting behavior of the particular solution as $t \to \infty$:
$$\ln N = 0.5\mathrm{e}^{-0.02t} + \ln 1000 - 0.5$$
As $t \to \infty$, the decaying exponential term approaches zero: $\mathrm{e}^{-0.02t} \to 0$.

Therefore, the logarithm of the population approaches:
$$\ln N \to \ln 1000 - 0.5$$

Exponentiate to find the limiting population:
$$N \to \mathrm{e}^{\ln 1000 - 0.5} = 1000\mathrm{e}^{-0.5} = \dfrac{1000}{\sqrt{\mathrm{e}}} \approx 607$$
